correctness.rationale: For every contractive matrix-valued Drury–Arveson multiplier, applying the multiplier to a constant vector gives ||A_alpha|| <= sqrt(|alpha|!/alpha!). For the normalized monomial e_alpha, its weighted shift coefficient at e_beta has squared size product_j binom(alpha_j+beta_j,alpha_j)/binom(|alpha|+|beta|,|alpha|) <= 1 by multivariate Vandermonde; the vacuum coefficient is exactly 1. The diagonal direct sum of all nonconstant e_alpha is therefore a norm-one multiplier and achieves every coefficient bound at once. The polynomial-growth Cauchy–Schwarz estimate proves finite-dimensional convergence; the finite-degree and finite-matrix witnesses prove nonradiality and the displayed counterexample. The proof treats countable-dimensional variables and possible divergent pointwise majorants explicitly. The included checker passed 52,012 supplementary finite assertions; no infinite claim depends on their exhaustiveness.

evidence: arXiv:2111.11713, Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.2 claim a radius of 1/sqrt(2) for operator-valued zero-constant bounded functions. Their class contains diag(z,z^2), which has norm max(|z|,|z|^2)<1 on the disk yet majorant 10/9 at |z|=2/3<1/sqrt(2). Thus that asserted broader inequality is not mathematically applicable as a valid dominating result.

value.rationale: The 2026 scalar complete-Pick Bohr-set classification makes matricial stability a directly motivated question. The result gives an exact complete pointwise classification for the entire zero-constant contractive matrix-valued multiplier class, not a one-off example; it shows non-Euclidean geometry and dimension collapse, and exhibits a concrete finite-dimensional obstruction to an earlier asserted operator-valued 1/sqrt(2) threshold. A sharp 1/2 one-variable threshold and the all-dimensional multinomial-weighted series offer meaningful boundaries for future operator-space versions of Bohr estimates. Mathematical value does not rely on code or on novelty searches alone.
